messages:
Sam H: Heads up — since the kernel-selector change (deploy 1.3.2) we’ve been seeing periodic 95/99 tail jumps on /v1/generate (hosted). Not consistent across models but spikes line up with tiny micro-batches.
Maya R: ack. Are these visible in the token-level breakdown dash? can you paste the route filter?
Sam H: yes, per-route KPIs show a bump in token_latency_p90/p99 when batch_size <= 4. Route filter: route="/v1/generate" && model=~".*-smallbatch.*"
Kevin L: ran a quick profiler during a noisy window. Summary:
```
kernel_dispatch_time_ms: normal
kernel_choice_switches: high (saw switch-from-fast->compat in 30% of small batches)
kv_cache_miss_rate: spike ~3x for same windows
queue_wait_ms (micro): also spiky
``` 
Kevin L: looks like small-batch shapes trigger a fallback kernel that has worse per-token path and also stales KV access patterns.
Tina S: interesting — might be two interacting signals: 1) kernel selector scoring prefers compatibility kernel when batch_len distribution is skewed, 2) KV cache eviction/rehash thrash during the same windows. Combined they amplify token-level latency.
perf-bot: regression-alert: metric=token_latency_p99, delta=+48%, window=5m, compare=baseline-1d. See: https://perf.redwood/alerts/1897654321
Sam H: attaching a short query we used to correlate kernel switches w/ latency. we should add this panel to the continuous-batching dashboard.
```
# PromQL-ish
sum by (route) (rate(kernel_switches_total{env="prod"}[1m]))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, route) (rate(token_latency_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])))
sum by (route) (increase(kv_cache_miss_total{env="prod"}[5m]))
``` 
Maya R: nice. I also want token-path breakdown at per-token position (first/median/last) — that will tell if KV cache coldness is hitting later tokens.
Sam H: agree, add panel: token_latency_by_position{route="/v1/generate"} split into p10/p50/p90/p99, overlay kernel_switch_rate.
Kevin L: quick mitigation proposal:
- raise kernel-selector compatibility_threshold for <8-token batches to prefer fast kernel
- smooth KV cache evictions by extending local-LRU grace time by 200ms
- temporarily increase batching max-wait to 8ms to let batches coalesce
I can prototype a patch for the selector weights and a runtime flag to flip.
Tina S: prefer telemetry-first approach: instrument the selector decisions (selector_reason label) + emit chosen_kernel and candidate_score_histogram. Then do a short canary with the compatibility_threshold change.
Sam H: agreed. also want an alert rule: if kernel_switch_rate(route="/v1/generate") > 5/min and kv_cache_miss_rate > 1/min for >10m then page @oncall.
Maya R: dashboard updates I'll make:
- new panel: "kernel_switch_rate vs token_p99 (route)" stacked
- heatmap: batch_size_histogram by route (0..64)
- time series: queue_wait_ms (p50/p90/p99) annotated with deploys
I’ll open a PR with Grafana JSON and the panel queries.
perf-bot: scheduled capture: profiler-job id=pf-20260318-02, collects: kernel-trace, kv-sampler, batchshape-sampler for 10m
infra-bot: deploy 1.3.2 rolled at 2026-03-18T09:12Z by ci/cd. Rollback token available if needed.
Kevin L: estimate: selector-weight patch + flag + canary = ~2h work + 30m canary; KV grace change needs a small runtime patch + 1h. I'll start on selector patch now.
Sam H: thanks. after changes we should run the perf-bot capture and compare token_latency histograms (pre/post). also add a small regression test: synthetic stream of small batches with KV warm/cold to detect path flip.
Tina S: will pair on the regression test. also adding a note to the runbook: when token_p99 jumps but batch_utilization low -> suspect kernel_selector + kv thrash interaction.
Maya R: tagging this for the continuous-batching epic. I’ll add the dashboard PR and the alert rule PR and link here.
Sam H: great. if we get a quick rollback signal we’ll revert 1.3.2; otherwise patch and canary in the next 2 hours. thanks all :thumbsup!
